_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible isocitrate dehydrogenase-1 (IDH1) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test.

pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory AML with an IDH1 mutation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Investigator-assessed CR + CRh (complete remission plus complete remission with partial hematologic recovery)
pivotal_trials.result: CR+CRh 51 (35%) [95% CI 27, 43]; median duration of CR+CRh 25.9 months [95% CI 13.5, NR]; CR 47 (32%) [95% CI 25, 40]

key_safety: Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions include transaminitis (20%), arthralgia, dyspnea, rash, nausea, and fatigue. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 25% of patients; those ≥5% included differentiation syndrome (9%) and transaminitis (6%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 1%, due to differentiation syndrome. Differentiation syndrome occurred in 16% (25/153), grade 3/4 in 8%.
target_moa: Olutasidenib is a small-molecule inhibitor of mutated IDH1; inhibition of IDH1 enzymes with gain-of-function mutations decreases 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) levels and induces myeloid differentiation.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: DIFFERENTIATION SYNDROME — Differentiation syndrome, which can be fatal, can occur with REZLIDHIA treatment. If suspected, withhold REZLIDHIA and initiate corticosteroids and hemodynamic monitoring until symptom resolution.

companion_dx_detail: IDH1 mutations in blood or bone marrow were confirmed using the Abbott RealTime IDH1 Assay (FDA-approved test for detection of IDH1 mutations).

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee or any other external consultants.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation for AML granted 27 April 2017.

summary.text: Olutasidenib received regular (full) approval as a standard-review NDA for R/R IDH1-mutated AML based on the single-arm Study 2102-HEM-101; the applicant's request for priority review was not granted, and the drug had Orphan Drug Designation for AML.

citations.quote: The review team recommends the regular approval of olutasidenib under 21 CFR 314.105 for the indication “treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a susceptible isocitrate dehydrogenase-1 (IDH1) mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test” using a dose of 150 mg twice daily. requirement.text: 4371-1: Conduct a clinical trial to confirm the appropriate dose of olutasidenib, and to assess safety, tolerability, PK, and PD in pediatric patients ages ≥12 to <18 years with IDH1-mutated gliomas.

citations.quote: 4371-1 Conduct a clinical trial to confirm the appropriate dose of olutasidenib, and to assess safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of

olutasidenib, in pediatric patients ages \ge 12 to <18 years with IDH1-mutated gliomas. Patients should be followed for at least 12 months (52 weeks). Include at least 6 patients \ge 12 to <18 years old.

requirement.text: 4371-2: Conduct a clinical drug interaction study to evaluate the effect of repeated doses of olutasidenib on the pharmacokinetics of substrates of OATP1B1.

citations.quote: 4371-2 Conduct a clinical drug interaction study to evaluate the effect of repeated doses of olutasidenib on the pharmacokinetics of substrates of OATP1B1. Assess the magnitude of increased drug exposure and determine appropriate dosage recommendations when olutasidenib is administered concomitantly with OATP1B1 substrates. Design and conduct the study in accordance with the FDA Guidance for Industry titled, "Clinical Drug Interaction Studies —Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions."

requirement.text: 4371-3: Conduct a study to further characterize the incidence and severity of differentiation syndrome, hepatotoxicity, and other serious toxicities with longer-term use of olutasidenib in patients with R/R AML (approximately 179 patients, followed for 3 years).

citations.quote: 4371-3 Conduct a study to further characterize the incidence and severity of differentiation syndrome, hepatotoxicity, and other serious toxicities that may develop with longer term use of olutasidenib, in patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML). This data may come from Study 2102-HEM-101. Include data from approximately 179 patients with relapsed or refractory AML that received olutasidenib as monotherapy. Patients should be followed for 3 years. Data should include exploratory subgroup analyses and corresponding subject level data that includes cytogenetics, specific IDH1 mutations, and mutation analyses for other genes as obtained under the study protocol.

requirement.text: 4371-4: Conduct a clinical drug interaction study to evaluate the effect of repeated doses of a moderate CYP3A inducer on the pharmacokinetics of olutasidenib.

Design and conduct the study in accordance with the FDA Guidance for Industry titled, "Clinical Drug Interaction Studies —Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions."
